{{C|Amplify}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Amplify}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Amplify}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Amplify}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy'''.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The first play of {{C|Heatsinks}} or {{C|Storm}} will already be activated by the second play.
** The first play of {{C|After Image}} will already give {{KW|Block}} because of the second play.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing a ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|Storm}} or {{BD|Heatsink}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.  

== Trivia ==
* Along with {{C|Double Tap}} and {{C|Burst}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.
* In [[Slay the Spire 2:Main|Slay the Spire 2]], this card was redesigned into {{C2|Signal Boost}}.
* This card's [[Beta Art]] shows the [[Defect]], [[Ironclad]], and [[Silent]] having a nice party. The [[Watcher]] was not invited.
** She was not in the game at this time.
** This card's [[Beta Art]] is likely a reference to the film ''Say Anything...''

{{BD|Artifact}} is a [[Buff]] that negates any debuff applied to the player. Each time a debuff is negated, a stack of {{BD|Artifact}} is removed.

== Sources ==
{{SortedQuery/all
| Keyword = Artifact
| Title = Player
| ShowDescriptions = true
| Where = KWP.Target = 'Player'
}}
{{SortedQuery/all
| Keyword = Artifact
| Title = Enemies
| ShowDescriptions = true
| Where = KWP.Target = 'Enemy'
}}

== Interactions ==
<!-- Could definitely expand this section. -->
* {{BD|Blasphemer}} is coded to act like a buff so that {{BD|Artifact}} and {{R|Orange Pellets}} cannot remove them.

=== Making temporary effects permanent ===
''(Copied from [[Strength#Making temporary effects permanent]])''
<!-- Need to include that this also works with Dexterity -->
* Temporary sources of {{BD|Strength}} like {{C|Flex}}, {{R|Mutagenic Strength}} and {{P|Flex Potion}} work by giving you {{BD|Strength}} plus an equal amount of {{BD|Strength Down}}. Since {{BD|Strength Down}} is a [[Debuff|debuff]], you can use {{BD|Artifact}} or {{R|Orange Pellets}} to remove it, keeping the gained {{BD|Strength}} permanently.
** {{BD|Artifact}} blocks each individual instance of {{BD|Strength Down}} gained, but can also prevent {{BD|Strength Down}} from working at the end of turn. Thus, if you have multiple {{P|Flex Potion|Flex Potions}}, it's better that you drink all of them '''before''' you gain {{BD|Artifact}}. This way you can block the {{BD|Strength Down}} of all potions combined with a single charge of {{BD|Artifact}}.

* Temporary sources of negative {{BD|Strength}} like {{C|Piercing Wail}} and {{C|Dark Shackles}} work by reducing {{BD|Strength}} then giving an equal amount of {{BD|Shackled}}. Since {{BD|Shackled}} is a [[Debuff|debuff]], it can be removed if applied on the same turn an enemy is removing debuffs, making the {{BD|Strength}} loss permanent.
** This trick works on {{M|The Champ}} using {{Int|The Champ|Anger}}, {{M|Awakened One}} using {{Int|Awakened One|Rebirth}} and {{M|Time Eater}} using {{Int|Time Eater|Haste}}.
** This does '''not''' work when {{M|Corrupt Heart}} is using {{Int|Corrupt Heart|Buff}}, because it doesn't remove debuffs, only negative {{BD|Strength}}. In fact, the {{M|Corrupt Heart}} will only end up ''stronger'' as the {{BD|Shackled}} remains while the negative {{BD|Strength}} doesn't.

title: Biased Cognition
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox |Name = Biased Cognition |Image = Blue-BiasedCognition.png |Color = Blue |Type = Power |Rarity = Rare |Cost = 1 |Description = Gain (4;5) {{BD|Focus}}.
At the start of your turn, lose 1 {{BD|Focus}}. |GivesToPlayer = Bias, Focus }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Bias |Image = Icon Bias.png |Description = At the start of your turn, lose X {{BD|Focus}}. |Type = Debuff |Stacks = Intensity |BetweenTurns = Permanent |Cap = Integer limit |GivesToPlayer = Focus (Negative) }} {{C|Biased Cognition}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}. == Interactions == === Order === * {{BD|Bias}} removes {{BD|Focus}} ''after'' the additional [[Orbs#Passive|Passives]] from {{C|Loop}} and {{R|Emotion Chip}} happen, despite the numbers on the Orbs changing visually first. * If an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} and a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} have already been played this turn, playing Biased Cognition may trigger {{R|Orange Pellets}}. If it does, {{BD|Bias}} will be cleared immediately. * In general, additive effects are applied before multiplicative ones. If a damaging Orb is improved by {{BD|Focus}} and then damages an enemy with {{BD|Lock-On}}, the {{BD|Focus}} will be added before the 50% increase from {{BD|Lock-On}}. === Synergies === * Like all sources of {{BD|Focus}}, Biased Cognition improves the output of {{KW|Lightning}}, {{KW|Frost}}, and {{KW|Dark}} Orbs. * Sources of {{BD|Focus}} stack, so Biased Cognition also works well with {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, and {{R|Data Disk}}. * {{BD|Bias}} is a [[Debuff]], and can be prevented with sources of {{BD|Artifact}} such as {{C|Core Surge}}, as well as removed by {{R|Orange Pellets}}. ** Note that the {{BD|Artifact}} has to be applied ''before'' Biased Cognition is played. Otherwise, the {{BD|Artifact}} will only consume the first removal of {{BD|Focus}}, if anything. ** On the other hand, {{R|Orange Pellets}} has to happen ''after'' the {{BD|Bias}} is applied, but this can be triggered by playing Biased Cognition itself. If {{R|Orange Pellets}} is activated on a subsequent turn, {{BD|Bias}} will still be cleared, but any {{BD|Focus}} lost in the interrim is not restored (unless you have negative {{BD|Focus}}). * {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy, and applies after {{BD|Focus}} for large damage output. === Neutral === * Stacking {{BD|Bias}} will result in losing multiple {{BD|Focus}} per turn. * {{KW|Plasma|Plasma Orbs}} are wholly unaffected by {{BD|Focus}}. * At first glance, it appears Biased Cognition will break even after 4 (5) turns. However, the value gained from {{BD|Focus}} in the meantime makes it take longer than that. Consider a simple example where you only have a single {{KW|Lightning}} Orb. If you play Biased Cogntition, it will deal 7 damage, then 6, then 5, etc. After 7 turns, you will have dealt 28 damage with Biased Cognition, and your {{BD|Focus}} will now be 0. On the other hand, if you hadn't played it, you'd deal 3 damage every turn, for a total of just 21 damage after 7 turns, and would still require another 3 turns to surpass the former example. === Anti-Synergies === * {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, undoing the benefit of Biased Cognition. However, as Biased Cognition will eventually remove all of its own {{BD|Focus}} anyway, {{C|Hyperbeam}} can still be useful as a finisher. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

When played, the card exhausts and causes Watcher to enter {{KW|Divinity|Divinity}}, which grants 3 {{Icon|PE}} Energy and triples the damage of your attacks for the rest of the turn. The price of this effect is that the Watcher becomes a {{BD|Blasphemer}}, ensuring 99999 self damage next turn. When upgraded, the card {{KW|Retain|Retains}}. == Interactions == === Synergies === * {{KW|Retain|Retaining}} attacks in hand such as {{C|Windmill Strike}} ensures you will have ammo for when {{C|Blasphemy}} is used. * {{BD|Vulnerable}} scales multiplicatively with {{KW|Divinity}} for a massive total 4.5x damage multiplier. * {{C|Blasphemy}} generates a lot of energy, which greatly benefits from card draw. * {{R|Lizard Tail}} and {{P|Fairy in a Bottle}} allows you to survive {{BD|Blasphemer}}. * As the upgraded version of {{C|Blasphemy}} {{KW|Retain|Retains}}, {{C|Establishment}} will decrease it in {{Icon|PE}}-cost at the end of a turn, unless it already costs 0. ==== Negating Blasphemer ==== Despite the card text of {{C|Blasphemy}} outright telling that it kills Watcher, it actually deals 99999 HP loss, which can be prevented. * {{R|Fossilized Helix}} completely blocks {{BD|Blasphemer}}. * {{BD|Intangible}} reduces {{BD|Blasphemer}} damage to 1. However, since {{BD|Intangible}} counts down at the beginning of your turn, you need at least 2 stacks to protect yourself. ** {{R|Incense Burner}} gives {{BD|Intangible}} at the beginning of your turn, so it can protect you even though it grants only 1 stack. Make sure its counter is on 5 the turn you play {{C|Blasphemy}}. ** Since {{BD|Blasphemer}} is HP loss, the 1 cannot be blocked by regular {{KW|Block}} cards. === Neutral === * {{C|Blasphemy}} does not generate {{BD|Mantra}}, so it does not scale up the damage of {{C|Brilliance}}. === Anti-Synergies === * {{BD|Blasphemer}} is intentionally treated as a "[[Buffs|positive buff]]" by the game, and thus cannot be blocked by {{BD|Artifact}} or removed with {{R|Orange Pellets}}. * Cards that change your {{KW|Stance}} will remove {{KW|Divinity}} without removing the {{BD|Blasphemer}} effect. * {{C|Conclude}}, {{C|Meditate}}, {{C|Vault}} and {{BD|Time Warp}} forcibly end your turn, likely resulting in your death. * Effects that play cards from your draw pile for free (like {{C|Mayhem}} and {{P|Distilled Chaos}}) may end up playing {{C|Blasphemy}} before you are ready. * {{BD|Invincible}} and {{BD|Unawakened}} may prevent you from ending the combat in one turn. == Trivia == * Max HP is not capped in Slay the Spire, which means it's possible (but unfeasible) to increase your HP so high you can survive {{BD|Blasphemer}}. ** One way this could be done is using 2 {{C|Nightmare|Nightmares}} to generate a large number of {{C|Nightmare|Nightmares}}, then using these cards to {{C|Wish}} for a massive quantity of [[Gold]], which can be used with {{R|The Courier}} to buy an endless amount of {{P|Fruit Juice}} at the [[Merchant]]. == Update History == {{Update History Table/start}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 10|* Adding polished card portrait for Blasphemy.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 7|* Blasphemy+ card now gives Retain on upgrade, cost remains at 1.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 5|* Blasphemy card now exhausts when played.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 2|* Tungesten Rod no longer stops Blasphemy from killing you. * Lightning strikes down the Blasphemer.}} {{Update History Table/row|Watcher 1|* Added XXX to the game ''(likely)''}} {{Update History Table/end}} {{WatcherNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Buffer}} is a 2 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Buffer}}, preventing the next instance(s) of losing HP.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion'''
** Fixed Self-Forming Clay relic triggering incorrectly off of prevented damage from Buffer power.

* '''Weekly Patch 49: The Designer'''
** Painful Stabs power will no longer give wounds if the damage was prevented by Buffer.

* '''Weekly Patch 44: Chrysalis'''
** Effects that trigger on damage like Masterful Stab now interacts properly with damage prevention effects like Buffer.

* '''Weekly Patch 35: Aggregate'''
** Buffer is no longer lost when hit by 0 damage attacks.
** Centennial Puzzle no longer draws cards when taking 0 damage as a result of things like Buffer.
** Shelled Parasite now accounts for Buffer and Intangible with its life leech action.

* '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World'''
** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game!
** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art.
** Content: 75 Cards.

{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Template:Under Construction}} {{Ambox|title=See Also| style="text-align:center; font-weight:bold;" ||color=red|icon=GremlinNob.png|message=''For information about Debuffs, see [[Debuffs]].''}}{{#setmainimage:Intent_Buff.png|quiet}} {{TOC limit|2}} == Stack Types == {{Hatnote|'''Note:''' These terms are not officially used by the game and are used by the wiki for better classification and description of their behavior.}} * '''Intensity buffs''' are more effective depending on how many stacks of the buff are applied. These buffs typically are either permanent for the combat encounter or are consumed on the following turn. * '''Duration buffs''' last for as many turns as there are stacks of the buff. At the end of the turn, the buff will decrement by one stack. * '''Counter buffs''' activate when an event happens, such as taking damage or being inflicted with a debuff. With the exception of {{BD|Mantra}}, counter buffs lose a stack each time they activate. * Buffs that do not stack are typically gained from Power cards and last the entire combat encounter. {{BD|Regen}} is the ONLY buff with both '''Intensity''' and '''Duration''' stack types. == Buffs == Characters may obtain buffs they may not normally cannot access by means of {{R|Prismatic Shard}} if it is obtained from a card.

wikitext:
{{Card Infobox |Name = Bullseye |Image = Blue-Bullseye.png |Color = Blue |Type = Attack |Rarity = Uncommon |Cost = 1 |Description = Deal (8;11) damage.
Apply (2;3) {{BD|Lock-On}}. |GivesToEnemy = Lock-On }} {{Power Infobox |Name = Lock-On |Image = Icon LockOn.png |Description = Receives 50% more damage from {{KW|Orb|Orbs}} for X turns. |Type = Debuff |Stacks = Duration |BetweenTurns = |Cap = |InteractsWith = Orb }} {{C|Bullseye}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}}. == Interactions == === Order === * In general, additive effects are applied before multiplicative ones. If a damaging Orb is improved by {{BD|Focus}} and then damages an enemy with {{BD|Lock-On}}, the {{BD|Focus}} will be added before the 50% increase from {{BD|Lock-On}}. === Synergies === * {{BD|Lock-On}} improves the damage of all {{KW|Lightning}} and {{KW|Dark}} Orb sources. * {{C|Electrodynamics}} is helpful in multi enemy combats for making sure the damage from {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} hits the enemy with {{BD|Lock-On}}. * Sources of {{BD|Focus}} apply before {{BD|Lock-On}}, allowing for large damage output: {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{R|Data Disk}}. * In addition to general Orb sources, cards that can manually {{KW|Evoke}} Orbs can be very useful for dealing damage with {{BD|Lock-On}}: {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, {{C|Multi-Cast}} ** {{C|Fission}} is a particular powerful option for this, allowing all of your damaging Orbs to be {{KW|Evoke|Evoked}} while the [[Debuff]] is active. === Anti-Synergies === * {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, reducing the damage output of your Orbs. == Trivia == * Bullseye is the only source in the game of {{BD|Lock-On}}. It is not unique in this regard, as {{BD|Mark}} has {{C|Pressure Points}} as its only source. * The art of Bullseye appears to be a {{KW|Lightning}} and {{KW|Dark}} Orb being fired at [[Donu]]. == Update History == * '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer''' ** Bullseye card buffed. Lock-On 1 -> 2. ** Bullseye+ card buffed. Damage 10 -> 11. * '''Switch Version 1.02''' ** Fixed Lock-On bug * '''Weekly Patch 40: Forethought''' ** Lock-On Power no longer incorrectly has the focused targeting effect. * '''Weekly Patch 39: We Meet Again!''' ** Lock-On card reworked. ** Lock-On card renamed -> Bullseye. * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

|BetweenTurns = 
|Cap          =

{{C|Burst}} is a 1 {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Burst}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Burst}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Burst}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards counts as a separate card being played, but this card is not added to your draw or discard pile, and is not {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} unless the card would {{KW|Exhaust}} upon being played normally. 

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|GE}} '''Energy'''. The second play of an X-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card will use the same value of X as the first.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The second play of {{C|Catalyst}} will multiply the {{BD|Poison}} that was already multiplied by the first play, effectively squaring the effect of the card.
** The second play of {{C|Calculated Gamble}} or {{C|Storm of Steel}} will [[Keywords#Discard|discard]] the cards that were respectively drawn or generated by the first play.

=== Synergies ===
* As {{C|Burst}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}, it can duplicate itself, resulting in more {{BD|Burst}}, which means more {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skills}} being duplicated.
** For example, if the player has no {{BD|Burst}} and plays {{C|Burst}}, {{C|Burst}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}} and {{C|Catalyst}}, in that order, the order of operations will be:
# The first {{C|Burst}} provides the player with the {{BD|Burst}} effect. 
# The second {{C|Burst}} is now played twice, consuming the initial {{BD|Burst}} but then providing 2 additional stacks of it. 
# {{C|Bouncing Flask}} is then played twice and one {{BD|Burst}} will be consumed.
# {{C|Catalyst}} is then played twice and the last {{BD|Burst}} will be consumed.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing a ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|After Image}} and {{BD|Thousand Cuts}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Letter Opener}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.

* Using {{BD|Burst}} on {{C|Blade Dance}} creates 6 (8 if {{C|Blade Dance}} is upgraded) {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} in hand, which can significantly advance counters on relics such as {{R|Shuriken}} and {{R|Nunchaku}} when played, but potentially exceeds the hand size limit in which case the remaining {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} will be added to the discard pile.

=== Anti-Synergies === 
* Since {{C|Panic Button}} immediately applies the {{BD|No Block}} debuff, using {{BD|Burst}} on {{C|Panic Button}} provides no extra {{KW|Block}}. 
* Since the first play of {{C|Expertise}} will fill the hand to the specified amount of cards, the second play will have no effect.

== Bugs ==
=== Bursting a Burst ===
On the Mobile version, there is a bug that can occur when Bursting a Burst. If you have exactly 1 stack of Burst, and you play Burst, then what happens is:
* The first play of Burst will occur, adding 1 (2) stacks.
* The game attempts to remove the stack of Burst that has been consumed. Due to a bug, it then removes '''all stacks of Burst, including the one(s) just added'''.
* The second play will happen, adding 1 (2) stacks.
Instead of ending up with 2 (4) stacks afterwards as expected, you will only have 1 (2), the same as if you hadn't Burst it at all.

If you have 2 or more stacks of Burst and play Burst, the game handles the interaction properly.

== Trivia ==

* Along with {{C|Double Tap}} and {{C|Amplify}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.

{{C|Collect}} is an X {{Icon|PE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Purple|Watcher}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives X (X+1 if upgraded) {{BD|Collect}}, which adds one upgraded {{C|Miracle}} to your hand at the start of every turn.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Collect}} takes effect before your cards are drawn. This means that it can cause you to draw less cards at the start of your turn due to the hand size limit.

=== Synergies ===
* {{R|Chemical X}} makes {{C|Collect}} apply 2 more times, regardless of the amount of {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' used to play it.
* If played through an effect such as {{P|Distilled Chaos}} or {{C|Omniscience}}, it will play for the full current {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' without actually using any.
* Can be used with 0 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' to advance {{R|Ink Bottle}} or {{R|Letter Opener}}.

=== Neutral ===
* If {{C|Collect}} is duplicated with an effect such as a {{P|Duplication Potion}} or {{C|Burst}}, the value of X will also be used for the copy.
* Being an X-cost, {{C|Collect}} can be {{C|Recycle|Recycled}} to double the current {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy'''.
* It will not count as a 0-cost card for {{C|Scrape}} or {{C|All for One}}.
* If a {{C|Miracle}} generated by this card exceeds your hand size limit, it gets added to the discard pile.

Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn. ** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected. * If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn. ** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn. * If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn. * If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking. Corpse Explosion applies the {{BD|Poison}}, then the {{BD|Corpse Explosion}} to the target. If the target has 1 stack of {{BD|Artifact}}, the {{BD|Corpse Explosion}} will go through. === Synergies === * {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}. * {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target. * {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die. * {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}. * {{C|Corpse Explosion}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}: ==== Cards ==== * {{C|Deadly Poison}}, {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Envenom}}. ==== Relics and potions ==== * {{R|Twisted Funnel}}. * {{P|Poison Potion}}. === Neutral === * {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process. * {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}. ** The damage dealt by Corpse Explosion going off also bypasses Flight, but not {{KW|Block}}. * However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}. === Anti-Synergies === * {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}} and {{BD|Corpse Explosion}}. ** However, as Corpse Explosion applies 2 [[Debuffs]] to the target for one card play, it can be very effective at clearing {{BD|Artifact}} for your other {{BD|Poison}} cards. * Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}. == Trivia == * This card is most likely a reference to the Diablo II Necromancer Corpse Explosion ability; in addition to have the exact same name, the mechanics of the card are also the same (deal damage to other enemies based on the health of the target) == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 51: Recursion''' ** Adding beta art for Bane, Charge Battery, Fission, Choke, Corpse Explosion, and Equilibrium. ** Fixed Corpse Explosion card's portrait using incorrect card type. * '''Weekly Patch 35: Aggregate''' ** Corpse Explosion power is now a debuff. * '''Weekly Patch 33: Terror''' ** Corpse Explosion power can now trigger on Darklings. ** Updating Power icon for Corpse Explosion. * '''Weekly Patch 32: Face Trader''' ** Rework: Corpse Explosion card: Apply 6 Poison. When this enemy dies, deal damage to ALL enemies equal to its max HP. * '''Weekly Patch 6: We're Back!''' ** Corpse Explosion is now affected by Powers (Vulnerable, Strength, Pen Nib, etc) * '''Weekly Patch 3: Balance Balance Balance''' ** Corpse Explosion card's type is now Attack. {{SilentNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Creative AI}} is a 3 (2 if upgraded) {{Icon|BE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives you one {{BD|Creative AI}}, which adds 1 {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card into your hand at the start of each turn. 

{{BD|Creative AI}} can only generate {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards you can find in card rewards through character choice or custom run modifiers, and is not affected by {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Creative AI}} takes effect before your cards are drawn. This means that having a high amount of {{BD|Creative AI}} can cause you to draw less cards at the start of your turn due to the hand size limit.

=== Synergies ===
* Synergizes with {{C|Storm}} and {{C|Heatsinks}} which get activated every time a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card is played. Both of these cards can also be generated by {{BD|Creative AI}}.
* Synergizes with {{C|Force Field}}, as it ensures enough {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} will be available to eventually lower the cost of {{C|Force Field}} to 0, and already discounts it by 1 {{Icon|BE}} '''Energy''' itself.
* Synergizes extremely well with power-dependent relics, as {{R|Mummified Hand}} makes it easier to play all generated {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards, and {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}} allows you to heal to full HP if combat lasts long enough.

=== Neutral ===
* If a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card generated by this card exceeds your hand size limit, it gets added to the discard pile.
* Some {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} cards cannot be generated, as they have some permanent effect out of combat, or can only be obtained from another source.

=== Excluded Cards ===
As with most random card generation effects, {{C|Creative AI}} cannot generate cards that are unobtainable from card rewards or cards that can heal the player. The following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} will never be generated by {{C|Creative AI}}:
* {{C|Self Repair}} (healing)
* {{C|Omega}} (can only be generated during combat via {{C|Alpha}} and {{C|Beta}})
* All {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless&type:Power|Colorless powers}} ({{C|Creative AI}} will only generate {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Powers}} of the player character's color and is not affected by {{R|Prismatic Shard}})

wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}}

|Cap          = -999 to 999 
|GivesToPlayer = Block

{{BD|Dexterity}} is a [[Buff]] that increases the amount of {{KW|Block}} you gain from cards. This '''does not''' apply to any other sources of {{KW|Block}}, only cards.

{{BD|Dexterity}} can be negative, reducing the {{KW|Block}} gained from cards to a minimum of 0.

== Sources ==
=== On Player ===
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Footwork}}: Gain 2({{TS|green||3}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}.
* {{C|Reprogram}}: Lose 1 {{BD|Focus}}. Gain 1({{TS|green||2}}) {{BD|Strength}}. Gain 1({{TS|green||2}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}.
* {{C|Wraith Form}}: Gain 2({{TS|green||3}}) {{BD|Intangible}}. At the end of your turn, lose 1 {{BD|Dexterity}}.
** Applies the {{BD|Wraith Form}} debuff.

==== Relics ====
* {{R|Kunai}}: Every time you play 3 {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} in a single turn, gain 1 {{BD|Dexterity}}.
* {{R|Oddly Smooth Stone}}: At the start of each combat, gain 1 {{BD|Dexterity}}.
* {{R|Duality}}: Whenever you play an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}}, gain 1 temporary {{BD|Dexterity}}.
** Also applies the {{BD|Dexterity Down}} debuff.

==== Potions ====
* {{P|Dexterity Potion}}: Gain 2(4 with {{R|Sacred Bark}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}.
* {{P|Speed Potion}}: Gain 5(10 with {{R|Sacred Bark}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}. At the end of your turn, lose 5(10 with {{R|Sacred Bark}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}.
** Applies the {{BD|Dexterity Down}} debuff.

==== Monsters ====
<!-- Make consistent with the descriptions in the Enemies database. Hover over the intent templates to see them. -->
* {{M|Lagavulin}}
** {{Int|Lagavulin|Siphon Soul}} - Player {{TS|negative||loses}} 1 ({{Asc|19|2}}) {{BD|Dexterity}}.

== Interactions ==
* Dexterity Does not affect block gained from [[Relics]] and {{KW|Frost}} Orbs.
* Dexterity does not affect block gained from Buffs or Debuffs, including those gained by {{C|Metallicize}}, {{C|Rage}}, {{C|Talk to the Hand}}, and {{C|After Image}}.
* Dexterity Does not affect block gained from {{C|Entrench}} or {{C|Wallop}}.
* {{C|Dodge and Roll}}'s {{BD|Next Turn Block}} depends on current turn effects, so if {{C|Dodge and Roll}} (at 0 {{BD|Dexterity}}) is played this turn and {{BD|Dexterity}} goes negative, the player will still gain 4 {{KW|Block}} next turn.
* Negative {{BD|Dexterity}} is treated as a debuff, so it can be removed with {{BD|Artifact}} or {{R|Orange Pellets}}.

=== Making Temporary Dexterity Permanent ===
{{Power Infobox
|Name         = Dexterity Down
|Image        = Icon StrengthDown.png
|Description  = At the end of this turn, lose X {{BD|Dexterity}}.
|Type         = Debuff
|Stacks       = Intensity
|BetweenTurns = 
|Cap          = 
}}
* Temporary sources of {{BD|Dexterity}} like {{R|Duality}} and {{P|Speed Potion}} work by giving you {{BD|Dexterity}} plus an equal amount of {{BD|Dexterity Down}}. Since it is a [[Debuff]], you can use {{BD|Artifact}} or {{R|Orange Pellets}} to remove it, keeping the gained {{BD|Dexterity}} permanently.

|Description  = Your next X {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} are played twice this turn.
|Type         = Buff
|Stacks       = Counter
|BetweenTurns = 
|Cap          = 
}}
{{C|Double Tap}} is a 1 {{Icon|RE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Red|Ironclad}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) stacks of {{BD|Double Tap}}, which will make the following {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card(s) this turn play twice, for the first amount of cards equal to the amount of {{BD|Double Tap}}. 

Having more than 1 {{BD|Double Tap}} will not increase the amount of times a single {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card is duplicated, but increases the amount of cards that can be duplicated when played.

The second play of these cards counts as a separate card being played, but this card is not added to your draw or discard pile, and is not {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} unless the card would {{KW|Exhaust}} upon being played normally. 

The second play of these cards does not expend any {{Icon|RE}} '''Energy'''. The second play of an X-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card will use the same value of X as the first.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* The second play of an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card only starts after the first play is fully resolved. In effect, it is as if the two cards were played with a pause in between, resulting in interactions including but not limited to:
** The second play of {{C|Headbutt}} will be able to target the first play in the discard pile. 
** {{BD|Vigor}} will be consumed by the first play, and will not be used for the second play.
** {{BD|Strength}} gained by {{R|Shuriken}} by the first play will already affect the second play.
** {{BD|Malleable}} will already give the target {{KW|Block}} after the first play.

=== Neutral ===
* The second play of an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} card counts as the play of a wholly separate card. All consequences of playing that card will still apply:
** The effects of the card itself.
** Anything that triggers or increments upon playing an ({{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}}) card, including but not limited to: 
*** Effects such as {{BD|Rage}}.
*** Relics such as {{R|Shuriken}} and {{R|Ink Bottle}}.
*** Card limits such as {{R|Velvet Choker}} and the Time Eater's {{BD|Time Warp}}.  

== Trivia ==

* Along with {{C|Burst}} and {{C|Amplify}}, one of the three 'play a card twice' Skills in the game.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 46: Adrenaline'''
** Fix for proper behavior when duplicating cards like Rampage and Genetic Algorithm with effects like Echo Form.

* '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot'''
** Updating icon for Double Tap power.

* '''Weekly Patch 28: The Ritual'''
** Fixed issue where cards stayed after combat with Echo Form or Double Tap.

If the first play of a card doubled this way kills its target, it will not count towards that X. == Interactions == === Synergies === * Playing an {{C|Echo Form}} as the first card of a turn where you have an {{BD|Echo Form}} will result in you getting 3 {{BD|Echo Form}} total, meaning the next 2 cards you play will both be doubled. * Cards that scale upon being played, such as {{C|Claw}} and {{C|Genetic Algorithm}} will scale twice if doubled by {{BD|Echo Form}}. * Cards with {{KW|Fatal}} effects, such as {{C|Ritual Dagger}}, will trigger their {{KW|Fatal}} effect even if only the second play was {{KW|Fatal}}. * The second play of an X-cost card will use the same value of X as the first. === Neutral === * Other doubling effects, such as from {{C|Amplify}}, do not apply to the second play of a card doubled with {{BD|Echo Form}}. ** For example, if you have two {{BD|Amplify}} and play a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} card with an {{BD|Echo Form}} active, that card will be played three times: once normally, which gets doubled by the first {{BD|Amplify}}, and once through {{BD|Echo Form}}, which will not get doubled by the second {{BD|Amplify}}. * The card played by {{C|Mayhem}} will be doubled by the first stack of {{BD|Echo Form}}, and consume that first stack. * The second play of a card doubled by {{BD|Echo Form}} counts as a card played. ** It will activate or increase the counter of relics triggered by that card, such as {{R|Velvet Choker}}, {{R|Ink Bottle}}, {{R|Letter Opener}} or {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}}. ** It will count towards relevant effects, such as {{BD|Beat of Death}}, The Awakened One's {{BD|Curiosity}}, {{BD|Hex}} or {{BD|Rage}}. === Anti-Synergies === * Using {{R|Blue Candle}} to {{KW|Exhaust}} a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} or {{R|Medical Kit}} to {{KW|Exhaust}} a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} will cause it to be doubled by the first stack of {{BD|Echo Form}}, and consume that first stack. In the case of {{R|Blue Candle}}, this will also cause you to lose 1 HP twice instead of only once. == Update History == * '''Weekly Patch 46: Adrenaline''' ** Fix for proper behavior when duplicating cards like Rampage and Genetic Algorithm with effects like Echo Form. * '''Weekly Patch 28: The Ritual''' ** Fixed issue where cards stayed after combat with Echo Form or Double Tap. * '''Weekly Patch 27: Hello World''' ** This week adds the long anticipated third character into the game! ** A new character with unique mechanics, keywords, and art. ** Content: 75 Cards. {{DefectNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Envenom}} is a 2 (1) {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* If {{C|Bane}} is played on an enemy with no {{BD|Poison}}, 1 will be added by the first hit of Bane, causing the second hit to occur.
* Although the {{BD|Poison}} applied by Envenom happens at the same time as the hit that caused it (i.e. before the next hit of the Attack), all triggers of {{C|Sadistic Nature}} will be applied after the attack finishes.

==== Poison Interactions ====
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* Attacks with multiple hits will trigger Envenom multiple times; for example, {{C|Riddle with Holes}}, {{C|Dagger Spray}}, and {{C|Skewer}}.
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}. It applies to each instance of {{BD|Poison}} separately. For instance, if you have Envenom and Snecko Skull, and hit an enemy with {{C|Glass Knife}}, that enemy will get 4 {{BD|Poison}}, not 3.

* {{C|Envenom}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Deadly Poison}}, {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The Attack does have to actually deal damage. If the {{M|Corrupt Heart}}'s {{BD|Invincible}} cap is maxed out for the turn, additional Attacks will not apply any {{BD|Poison}} to it.
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}.
** However, certain Attacks allow Envenom to deal several [[Debuffs]] in a single card play, clearing {{BD|Artifact}} for your other {{BD|Poison}} sources.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==
* '''Patch V1.1: The Dealer'''
** Envenom's Poison is now applied immediately after the damage occurs.

* '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot'''
** Updating icon for Envenom power.

* '''Weekly Patch 5: Happy Holidays!'''
** Envenom card gets a wording update for clarity.
** Updating description for Envenom power to mention unblocked dmg.

It gives one {{BD|Establishment}}, which lowers the {{Icon|PE}}-cost of all {{KW|Retain|Retained}} cards by one at the end of every turn they are {{KW|Retain|Retained}}. When upgraded, it becomes {{KW|Innate}}, meaning it will always appear in your first hand of combat.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Meditate}}, {{C|Well-Laid Plans}} and {{C|Equilibrium}} are cards that allow you to {{KW|Retain}} other cards and synergize well with {{C|Establishment}}, as they allows you to make any card cost 0 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' eventually.

* Cards that have an {{Icon|PE}}-cost above 0 and {{KW|Retain}} on their own benefit from this card:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Flying Sleeves}}, {{C|Protect}}, {{C|Perseverance}} and {{C|Windmill Strike}}
* {{C|Crescendo}} and {{C|Tranquility}}, although these already cost 0 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' when upgraded, meaning they then no longer benefit.
* {{C|Sands of Time}} will decrease in {{Icon|PE}}-cost an additional time for every stack of {{BD|Establishment}}.
* {{C|Worship}} and {{C|Blasphemy}}, only if upgraded.
* {{C|Safety}} from {{C|Deceive Reality}}, and {{C|Smite}} from {{C|Battle Hymn}} or {{C|Carve Reality}}.

=== Neutral ===
* {{R|Runic Pyramid}} does not {{KW|Retain}} cards, but prevents them from being [[Keywords#Discard|discarded]]. As a result of this, {{BD|Establishment}} does not reduce the cost of cards kept in hand through {{R|Runic Pyramid}} unless those cards are also under another actual {{KW|Retain}} effect.

It gives 5 (7 if upgraded) {{BD|Like Water}}, which gives that amount of {{KW|Block}} at the end of your turn if you are in the {{KW|Calm}} {{KW|Stance}} at that moment.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* As {{BD|Like Water}} gives {{KW|Block}} at the end of your turn, it does not prevent {{R|Orichalcum}} from activating.

=== Synergies ===
* Depends on being in {{KW|Calm}}, meaning it synergizes with ways to enter that {{KW|Stance}}:

==== Cards ====
* {{C|Vigilance}} can reliably make you enter {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{C|Tranquility}} can make you enter {{KW|Calm}} once at any point after first drawing it, making it a good fallback.
* {{C|Fear No Evil}} cannot reliably make you enter {{KW|Calm}}. However, in most cases the {{KW|Block}} from {{BD|Like Water}} is only needed if there is an enemy attacking, in which case this does work.
* {{C|Inner Peace}} synergizes well, as it allows you to enter {{KW|Calm}} and still receive full benefits from itself while remaining in {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{C|Meditate}} reliably ensures you are in {{KW|Calm}} at the end of your turn.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Teardrop Locket}} makes you start combat in {{KW|Calm}}.
* {{P|Stance Potion}} allows you to pick between entering {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Wrath}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The {{KW|Block}} gained by {{BD|Like Water}} is unaffected by {{BD|Frail}}, {{BD|Dexterity}} or {{BD|No Block}} from a previously played {{C|Panic Button}}.

== Interactions ==

=== Synergies ===
* While all of the Orb types benefit from Loop, {{KW|Dark|Dark Orbs}} particularly benefit from the additional [[Orbs#Passive|Passives]], allowing them to grow quickly: {{C|Darkness}}, {{C|Doom and Gloom}}, {{C|Chaos}}, {{C|Rainbow}}, {{R|Symbiotic Virus}}, {{P|Essence of Darkness}}

* In addition to general Orb sources, cards that can manually {{KW|Evoke}} the first Orb can be very useful for setting up Loop on the correct Orb: {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, {{C|Multi-Cast}}
** {{C|Fission}} may be used in a similar fashion, but requires {{KW|Channel|Channeling}} the Orb you want afterwards.

{{C|Mayhem}} is a 2 (1 if upgraded) {{Icon|CE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives one {{BD|Mayhem}}, which plays the top card of your draw pile at the start of every turn, without expending any {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy'''. X-cost cards will use your current {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy''' for X, without consuming that {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy'''.

== Obtaining Mayhem ==
{{C|Mayhem}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways:
* Can be bought from the [[Merchant]].
* Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected.
* Can be obtained from [[Monsters]], [[Elites]] and [[Bosses]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.
** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers.
* Can be obtained from Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a negative effect.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Mayhem}} activates ''after'' drawing cards at the start of the turn, meaning that something that is placed on top of your draw pile at the end of your previous turn will not be played through {{BD|Mayhem}} but drawn as normal.
* If you have {{BD|Echo Form}}, the card played by {{C|Mayhem}} will be played twice by that {{BD|Echo Form}} and consume it for that turn.

=== Synergies ===
* {{R|Frozen Eye}} allows you to see which card {{C|Mayhem}} will target.
* {{C|Mayhem}} will play X-cost cards for their full {{Icon|CE}} '''Energy''' without actually using any.

=== Neutral ===
* Playing a {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} card via {{BD|Mayhem}} will place the card into your discard pile, bypassing end-of-turn negative effects from cards such as {{C|Doubt}} and {{C|Burn}}, but also preventing {{KW|Ethereal}} cards such as {{C|Ascender's Bane}} and {{C|Dazed}} from being {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}}.
** If you have {{R|Medical Kit}} or {{R|Blue Candle}}, respectively {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Status}} or {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} will be {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausted}} when they are played by {{BD|Mayhem}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* Generally, there is little control over which card is played by {{BD|Mayhem}}. This means cards with possible negative effects, such as {{C|Offering}}, {{C|Eruption}} or {{C|Blasphemy}} can be played, or cards that need to be played at a specific time for maximum effect, such as {{C|Limit Break}} or {{C|Apparition}} can be wasted.

It gives 4 (6 if upgraded) {{BD|Mental Fortress}}, which gives that amount of {{KW|Block}} every time you switch {{KW|Stance}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* When changing your {{KW|Stance}} as a result of a card, {{BD|Mental Fortress}} will activate before the card is fully resolved, meaning it can already {{KW|Block}} damage such as from {{BD|Beat of Death}}.

=== Synergies ===
* Anything that can cause you to switch {{KW|Stance}} will synergize with this card:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Empty Body}}, {{C|Empty Fist}} and {{C|Empty Mind}}, as long as you were in a {{KW|Stance}} previously.

* As long as you were not in {{KW|Wrath}} previously, {{C|Eruption}}, {{C|Crescendo}}, {{C|Indignation}}, {{C|Simmering Fury}} and {{C|Tantrum}}.

*  As long as you were not in {{KW|Calm}} previously, {{C|Vigilance}}, {{C|Tranquility}}, {{C|Fear No Evil}}, {{C|Inner Peace}} and {{C|Meditate}}.
** {{C|Fear No Evil}} will only work if it is played on a target that [[Intent|Intends]] to attack.

* As long as you were not in {{KW|Divinity}} previously, {{C|Prostrate}}, {{C|Pray}}, {{C|Worship}} and {{C|Devotion}} can give you enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}}, and {{C|Blasphemy}} can do it directly.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Damaru}} can give you enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}}.
* {{P|Stance Potion}} will always give you the possibility to switch {{KW|Stance}}, no matter what your current {{KW|Stance}} is.
* As long as you were not in {{KW|Divinity}} previously, {{P|Ambrosia}}.

=== Neutral ===
* The {{KW|Block}} gained by {{BD|Mental Fortress}} is unaffected by {{BD|Frail}}, {{BD|Dexterity}} or {{BD|No Block}} from a previously played {{C|Panic Button}}.

{{BD|Minion}} is a [[Buff]] that is automatically applied to [[Monsters|Enemies]] who are spawned by other Enemies.

== Effects ==
Despite being a Buff, {{BD|Minion}} does not grant any positive effects to Enemies that have it. Instead, it does the following:
* Enemies with {{BD|Minion}} will flee the battle when all non-Minion Enemies die.
* Cards with effects granted by {{KW|Fatal}} will not trigger if used to kill a {{BD|Minion}}.

Cannot use {{Int|Nemesis|Tri Attack}} three times in a row. == Found With == === Act 3 === * Solo == Lore == When completing the Act 3 event {{E|Sensory Stone}}, you 'recall' what appear to be memories regarding the pasts of the characters. The {{TS|green||TRIUMPH}} dialogue option may recall a battle between the [[Silent]] and the [[Nemesis]], and her reason for climbing the Spire.
{{TS|green|up|TRIUMPH}}
The remains of a {{TS|purple|up|ghostly creature}} sink slowly into the mud before you, barely visible in the moonlight. You have proven yourself amongst your sisters.
Standing victoriously, you wait in silence as the others ceremoniously place the {{TS|gold||creature's skull}} atop your head. The ritual has concluded.
You head towards the Spire...

{{C|Noxious Fumes}} is a 1 {{Icon|GE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Green|Silent}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

=== Synergies ===
* {{C|Bane}} does additional damage if the target has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} can double (triple) the amount of {{BD|Poison}} on a target.
* {{R|The Specimen}} can be used in combats with multiple enemies to consolidate {{BD|Poison}} as enemies die.
* {{R|Snecko Skull}} applies 1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever this card applies {{BD|Poison}}.

* {{C|Noxious Fumes}} works well with other sources of {{BD|Poison}}:
==== Cards ====
* {{C|Poisoned Stab}}, {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, {{C|Crippling Cloud}}, {{C|Noxious Fumes}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}}, {{C|Envenom}}.

==== Relics and potions ====
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}.
* {{P|Poison Potion}}.

=== Neutral ===
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* {{BD|Poison}} bypasses {{KW|Block}} and {{BD|Flying}}.
* However, {{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{BD|Artifact}} will prevent applying {{BD|Poison}}. {{BD|Noxious Fumes}} will naturally clear out {{BD|Artifact}} over time.
* Certain bosses will remove all [[Debuffs]] during combat: {{M|The Champ}}, {{M|Awakened One}}, and {{M|Time Eater}}.

== Update History ==
* '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot'''
** Updating icon for Noxious Fumes power.

{{Intents Table/row

'''Orb Walker''' will use one of the following actions each turn:
* {{Int|Orb Walker|Laser}} (60% chance)
* {{Int|Orb Walker|Claw}} (40% chance)
'''Orb Walker''' cannot use either action three times in a row.

== In Party With ==
=== Act 3 ===
As an easy pool encounter:
* Solo

In the {{E|Mysterious Sphere}} [[Event]] alongside:
* 1 other '''Orb Walker'''

== Tips ==

* The Orb Walker scales strength somewhat quickly, with the added threat of diluting your draw pile with [[Burn|Burns]]. End the fight quickly and, if necessary, consider taking damage in early turns to play critical cards.
* {{BD|Weak}} is effective at blocking large amounts of damage if the fight is drawn out.

== Trivia ==
* '''Orb Walker''' appears in the artwork of {{C|Evaluate}}.

== Update History ==
* Weekly Patch 50: The Final Act
** Awakened One and Orb Walkers were not shuffling their status cards into the player's draw pile, but into a fixed position.

{{C|Panache}} is a 0 {{Icon|CE}} cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Rare|Rare}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It applies the {{BD|Panache}} effect on the player, which does 10 (14) damage to ALL enemies every time you play 5 cards in one turn. This effect can trigger more than once per turn, so for instance playing 10 cards in one turn will cause the damage to occur twice.

== Obtaining Panache ==
{{C|Panache}} is a {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} card, and therefore can be obtained in the following ways:
* Can be bought from the [[Merchant]].
* Can appear in the {{E|Sensory Stone}} event, from a choice of 3-9 {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Colorless|Colorless}} cards, depending on the option that is selected.
* Can be obtained from [[Monsters]], [[Elites]] and [[Bosses]] with {{R|Prismatic Shard}}.
** Also found in the [[Custom Mode|Daily Climb]] with the {{KW|Diverse}} or {{KW|Colorless Cards}} modifiers.
* Can be obtained from Neow's [[Third Blessing]] in exchange for a negative effect.

== Interactions ==
=== Synergies ===
Regardless of character, there exist ways to play infinite cards in a single turn, which naturally synergizes with Panache. As there are many different ways to go infinite, and most infinites generate damage even without Panache, for the rest of this section only finite strategies are listed.

==== As the Ironclad ====
[[Ironclad]] usually does not play very many cards in a turn, and so will rarely be able to proc Panache. 
* {{C|Corruption}} makes all Skills cost 0, allowing more cards to be played most turns.
* {{C|Offering}} and {{C|Seeing Red}} both generate {{Icon|RE}}, and may allow playing more cards in a turn.

==== As the Silent ====
[[Silent]] tends to play many cards at once fairly easily, and generally benefits the most from Panache.
* {{C|Shiv}} generation cards, especially {{C|Blade Dance}} and {{C|Storm of Steel}}, enable playing 5 cards for very little {{Icon|GE}}.
* {{C|Adrenaline}}, {{C|Concentrate}}, {{C|Outmaneuver}}, {{C|Flying Knee}} and {{C|Tactician}} all give you access to more Energy.
* {{C|Bullet Time}} makes your whole hand cost 0 temporarily.
* {{C|Choke}} does not directly enable more card plays, but it also benefits from many cards being played at once.

==== As the Defect ====
[[Defect]] primarily benefits from Panache when either using a 0-cost strategy or [[Orbs#Plasma Orbs|Plasma Orbs]].
* {{C|All for One}} and {{C|Scrape}} enable playing lots of 0 cost cards in a single turn.
* Sources of Plasma allow you to consistently have more {{Icon|BE}} each turn: {{C|Fusion}}, {{C|Meteor Strike}}, {{C|Chaos}}, and {{R|Nuclear Battery}}.
* Defect also has various other Energy generation methods: {{C|Double Energy}}, {{C|Aggregate}}, {{C|Fission}}, {{C|Recycle}}, and {{C|TURBO}}.

==== As the Watcher ====
[[Watcher]] has quite a lot of ways to generate both cards that cost 0 and {{Icon|PE}} (thanks in part to both {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Divinity}}).
* Sources of {{C|Miracle}}s: {{C|Collect}}, {{C|Deus Ex Machina}}, and {{R|Pure Water}}.
* Sources of {{KW|Scry}} allow you to manipulate your hand, avoiding drawing dead cards: {{C|Third Eye}}, {{C|Foresight}}, and {{C|Cut Through Fate}}.
* {{C|Scrawl}} gives you access to many cards at once.
* {{C|Deva Form}} gives you a huge amount of Energy as combat goes on, enabling lots of card plays per turn consistently.

==== All Classes ====
* {{C|Enlightenment}} and {{C|Madness}} both reduce the cost of cards potentially allowing playing more cards per turn.
* {{C|Purity}} allows you to exhaust several cards at will, allowing the removal of {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Status|Statuses}} or unwanted cards like {{C|Strike (Ironclad)|Strike}}, allowing you to draw cheap cards more consistently.

==== Relics ====
* Any relic which gives Energy.
* {{R|Unceasing Top}} allows you to continuously draw more cards to play, assuming you have energy left.
* {{R|Mummified Hand}} makes cards temporarily free when playing Powers.
* Various relics benefit from playing lots of cards as well: {{R|Ornamental Fan}}, {{R|Letter Opener}}, {{R|Ink Bottle}}.

=== Neutral ===
==== Strength ====
Is completely unaffected by {{BD|Strength}}. This means the debuff from [[Spire Spear]] will have no effect on it, but neither will {{R|Shuriken}}, {{R|Vajra}}, or {{C|Inflame}}.

==== Thorns and Flight ====
As Panache does not do Attack damage, it bypasses {{M|Spiker|Spikers'}} {{BD|Thorns}} and {{M|Byrd|Byrds'}} {{BD|Flying}}, but it also does not benefit from {{M|Giant Head|Giant Head's}} {{BD|Slow}}.

==== Stances ====
Similarly, the damage from Panache is not affected by being in {{KW|Wrath}} or {{KW|Divinity}}. However, the Energy generated by entering Divinity may make it easier to proc the damage in the first place.

{{R|Pen Nib}} is a {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common}} [[Relic]]. The counter that keeps track of how many {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} have been played is not reset between turns or combats.

== Sources ==
* Can be dropped by fighting [[Elites]], by buying from the [[Merchant]], or found in a [[Small Chest]] or [[Medium Chest]]. See Chest and non-Chest chance at [[Relics#Rarity|Relics > Rarity]].
* Can be obtained from the relics {{R|Calling Bell}}, {{R|Shovel}}, {{R|Black Star}}, and {{R|Matryoshka}}.
** {{R|Calling Bell}}'s {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common}} relic can be {{R|Pen Nib}}.
** {{R|Matryoshka}}'s extra relic has a 75% chance of being {{QueryLink|Relics|rarity:Common|Common}}, which can be {{R|Pen Nib}}.
* Can be obtained from the following [[Events]]:
** {{E|We Meet Again!}}: Can give {{R|Pen Nib}} in exchange for either a [[Potion]], some [[Gold]], or a [[Card]].
** {{E|Wheel of Change}}: Can drop {{R|Pen Nib}} as a prize.
** {{E|Big Fish}}: Can give {{R|Pen Nib}} along with {{C|Regret}}.
** {{E|Dead Adventurer}}: Either by choosing {{Frame|Search}} and getting {{R|Pen Nib}} as a reward, or by fighting the [[Elite]] (which can drop {{R|Pen Nib}}).
** {{E|Scrap Ooze}}: Can give {{R|Pen Nib}} with an X% chance, for increasing amounts of damage and likelihood of success on repeated attempts.
** {{E|Pleading Vagrant}}: Can give {{R|Pen Nib}} in exchange for either 85 [[Gold]] by choosing {{Frame|Offer Gold}}, or {{C|Shame}} by choosing {{Frame|Rob}}.
** {{E|The Mausoleum}}: Can give {{R|Pen Nib}} along with {{C|Writhe}}.

== Interactions ==

=== Order ===
When calculating damage dealt, all the additive bonuses are added first, and then multiplicative bonuses are multiplied. The final result is rounded down. {{R|Pen Nib}}'s {{BD|Pen Nib}} buff is a multiplicative bonus, and stacks with {{BD|Vulnerable}}.

=== Synergies ===
* {{R|Ninja Scroll}} allows for an easy +3 to {{R|Pen Nib}}'s counter at the start of every combat.
* {{R|Pen Nib}}'s buff applies to all hits from a single card, allowing multi-hit {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|attacks}} (such as {{C|Sword Boomerang}}, {{C|Flechettes}}, and {{C|Bowling Bash}}) to benefit from the increased damage for all their hits.
* Cards which generate multiple cheap {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} (such as {{C|Blade Dance}} and {{C|Storm of Steel}}) can contribute a lot of progress to {{R|Pen Nib}}'s counter.
** These cheap {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}} can be used to build up {{R|Pen Nib}}'s buff and then use it on a single devastating '''attack''', such as {{C|Ragnarok}} or {{C|Immolate}}.
* {{P|Attack Potion}} can be used flexibly to either find a random {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|attack}} that will activate {{R|Pen Nib}}'s buff for the next '''attack''', or find a big '''attack''' to take advantage of the buff itself.

=== Neutral ===
* {{C|Havoc}}, {{C|Mayhem}}, and {{P|Distilled Chaos}} can be used to potentially play a less desirable {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|attack}} from the draw pile and activate {{R|Pen Nib}}'s buff to be used on a more effective '''attack''' currently in the hand.
** This can potentially backfire if the player is attempting to dig for a big attack from their draw pile while the buff is active and ends up playing a low-damage attack instead, somewhat wasting the damage bonus.

== Trivia ==
* {{R|Pen Nib}} resembles the nib of a dip pen.<ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dip_pen</ref> It is a type of pen that must be physically dipped into ink, and the nib is responsible for depositing a small amount of ink onto the writing surface.
** Dip pens have their origins as far back as ancient Egypt, and are still manufactured and used today.

{{BD|Poison}} is a [[Debuff]] that the [[Silent]] can apply to Enemies.

At the beginning of its turn, an enemy with {{BD|Poison}} will lose HP equal to its number of {{BD|Poison}} stacks. Then, its {{BD|Poison}} stack will decrease by 1.

Damage applied by {{BD|Poison}} ignores enemy {{KW|Block}}, and each {{BD|Artifact}} stack will negate all {{BD|Poison}} applied by a single source. 

== Sources ==

==== Cards ====
* {{C|Deadly Poison}}: 5(7) {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Poisoned Stab}}: 3(4) {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Bouncing Flask}}: 3 {{BD|Poison}} to a random enemy 3(4) times.
* {{C|Crippling Cloud}}: 4(7) {{BD|Poison}} to all enemies.
* {{C|Corpse Explosion}}: 6(9) {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Noxious Fumes}}: 2(3) {{BD|Poison}} each turn to all enemies.
* {{C|Envenom}}: 1 {{BD|Poison}} each unblocked attack.
* {{C|Catalyst}}: Doubles(triples) existing {{BD|Poison}}.

==== Relics ====
* {{R|Snecko Skull}}: +1 {{BD|Poison}} whenever {{BD|Poison}} is applied. Works with {{R|The Specimen}}, but only works as +1 with {{C|Catalyst}}.
* {{R|The Specimen}}: Transfers {{BD|Poison}} from a defeated enemy to a random enemy. Can only transfer up to 9999 {{BD|Poison}} to a previously unpoisoned enemy.
* {{R|Twisted Funnel}}: 4 to all enemies at the start of combat.

==== Potions ====
* {{P|Poison Potion}}: 6 ({{R|Sacred Bark|12}}) {{BD|Poison}}.

== Synergies ==
* {{C|Bane}} will deal an additional 7(10) damage if the enemy has {{BD|Poison}}.
* {{C|Catalyst}} will double(triple) existing {{BD|Poison}}. 
* {{C|Sadistic Nature}} will deal 5(7) damage whenever {{BD|Poison}} is applied.

== Interactions ==
{{BD|Intangible}} reduces ''all'' sources of HP loss to 1, including {{BD|Poison}}.

As {{BD|Poison}} applies at the start of the enemy's turn, it has some unusual interactions:
* {{BD|Poison}} damage causes {{M|Lagavulin}} to wake up, consuming its Stunned turn in the process.
* If the damage is enough to cause {{M|The Guardian}} to change to Defensive form, it will immediately change its [[Intent]] to apply {{BD|Sharp Hide}}. Moreover, as it is already past the point in its turn where {{KW|Block}} is removed, it will keep the Block generated by moving to Defensive Form until its next turn.
** Notably, in other cases where HP thresholds affect enemy [[Intent]] (such as {{M|The Champ}} and {{M|Time Eater}}), this happens on a subsequent turn, and will not be affected.
* If the enemy dies to {{BD|Poison}}, the card drawn by {{R|Gremlin Horn}} will be held until your next turn.
** Similarly, if a {{M|Bronze Orb}} dies while holding a card in Stasis, that card will be returned to you and stay in your hand until next turn.
* If a {{M|Fungi Beast}} dies this way, you will receive {{BD|Vulnerable}} during the enemy turn, which may increase the amount of incoming damage for the turn.
* If an enemy with {{BD|Minion|Minions}} dies this way, its Minions will still flee combat before attacking.

== Achievements ==
=== CATALYST ===
* Unlocks when {{BD|Poison}} exceeds '''98''' on any target. 

=== PLAGUE ===
* Defeat 3 enemies with {{BD|Poison}} in a '''single combat'''.

title: Rupture
wikitext:
{{Sequel Disambiguation}} {{Card Infobox | Name = Rupture | Image = Red-Rupture.png | Color = Red | Type = Power | Rarity = Uncommon | Cost = 1 | Description = Whenever you lose HP from a card,
gain (1;2) {{BD|Strength}}. | GivesToPlayer = Rupture | PowerGives = Strength, Lose HP }} {{Power Infobox | Name = Rupture | Image = Icon Rupture.png | Description = Whenever you lose HP from a card, gain X {{BD|Strength}}. | Type = Buff | Stacks = Intensity | BetweenTurns = | Cap = | GivesToPlayer = Strength | InteractsWith = Lose HP }} {{C|Rupture}} is a 1 {{Icon|RE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Red|Ironclad}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives 1 (2 if upgraded) {{BD|Rupture}}, which gives that amount of {{BD|Strength}} whenever a card causes you to lose HP. == Interactions == === Order === * {{C|Hemokinesis}} will not benefit from the {{BD|Strength}} gained as a result of {{BD|Rupture}} until played again, as {{BD|Rupture}} triggers ''after'' the card is already resolved. * HP loss caused by {{C|Pain}} applies ''after'' the effects of the card that triggered it, meaning {{BD|Rupture}} will trigger ''after'' the card that triggered {{C|Pain}} has already dealt damage. ** However, if you have {{C|Pain}} in hand and use a different card to cause an {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} to be played, such as through {{C|Havoc}}, the first card will trigger {{C|Pain}} and therefore {{BD|Rupture}} ''before'' the {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} takes effect. === Synergies === * Playing any {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Curse|Curse}} with {{R|Blue Candle}} triggers {{BD|Rupture}}. * {{C|Reaper}} gives healing based on damage dealt, and therefore increases with {{BD|Strength}}. This can be used to regain HP lost as a result of triggering this card. * Any card that can cause you to lose HP can trigger {{BD|Rupture}}: ==== Cards ==== * {{C|Bloodletting}}, {{C|Hemokinesis}} and {{C|J.A.X.}} can repeatedly be played to trigger it. * {{C|Offering}} can be played to trigger it and then {{KW|Exhaust|Exhausts}}. * {{C|Combust}} and {{C|Brutality}} will trigger it every turn. * {{C|Regret}} will trigger it if it is in your hand at the end of your turn. * {{C|Pain}} makes every other card in hand cost 1 HP, allowing you to rack up large quantities of {{BD|Strength}} quickly. * {{C|Burn}} and {{C|Decay}} deal damage instead of causing HP loss directly. This will still trigger {{BD|Rupture}}, as long as the damage is not fully negated by {{KW|Block}}, and therefore causes you to lose HP. === Neutral === * The amount of {{BD|Strength}} gained from triggering {{BD|Rupture}} does not scale with the amount of HP lost. * Losing HP when playing a card, as a result of {{BD|Thorns}}, {{BD|Sharp Hide}} or {{BD|Beat of Death}}, will not trigger {{BD|Rupture}}. == Trivia == * Technically {{C|Blasphemy}} deals 99999 damage instead of killing the player directly. In theory this could be used to activate {{C|Rupture}}, although unpractical in reality. == Update History == * '''Patch V2.2: Happy Holidays!''' ** Rupture+ card buffed. Strength gain increased from 1 -> 2. ** Rupture+ card nerfed. Energy cost 0 -> 1. * '''Weekly Patch 42: Reboot''' ** Updating icon for Rupture power. {{IroncladNav}} [[Category:Cards]]

{{C|Rushdown}} is a 1 (0 if upgraded) {{Icon|PE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Purple|Watcher}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}} Card. It gives 2 {{BD|Rushdown}}, which makes you draw that amount of cards whenever you enter the {{KW|Wrath}} {{KW|Stance}}, as long as you were not in {{KW|Wrath}} before.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* If you enter {{KW|Wrath}} because of a card, that card will be placed into the discard pile, or draw pile in the case of {{C|Tantrum}}, before {{BD|Rushdown}} is triggered, meaning it is possible to immediately redraw that card.

=== Synergies ===
* Depends on being in {{KW|Wrath}}, meaning it synergizes with ways to enter that {{KW|Stance}}:

==== Cards ====
* {{C|Eruption}}, {{C|Indignation}} and {{C|Tantrum}} can reliably make you enter {{KW|Wrath}}.
* {{C|Crescendo}} can make you enter {{KW|Wrath}} once at any point after first drawing it, making it a good fallback.
* {{C|Simmering Fury}} triggers after you draw the start of your turn, and gives extra draw on top of that, meaning this has a high chance of already filling your hand before {{BD|Rushdown}} can be useful.

==== Potions ====
* {{P|Stance Potion}} allows you to pick between entering {{KW|Calm}} and {{KW|Wrath}}.

== Trivia ==
* During beta testing Rushdown was called Adaptation, and triggered on all Stance changes. The internal name is still Adaptation.

|Type         = Buff

{{Power Infobox|Draw Card}}
{{C|Simmering Fury}} is a 1 {{Icon|PE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Purple|Watcher}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Skill|Skill}} Card. It gives you one {{BD|Simmering Rage}}, which will make you enter the {{KW|Wrath}} {{KW|Stance}} at the start of your next turn. It also gives 2 (3 if upgraded) {{BD|Draw Card}}, which will make you draw that amount of extra cards at the start of next turn.

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* {{BD|Simmering Rage}} activates after {{BD|Mantra}} is given at the start of your turn. This means that if you get enough {{BD|Mantra}} to enter {{KW|Divinity}} through {{C|Devotion}} or {{R|Damaru}}, you will briefly enter {{KW|Divinity}} and then immediately enter {{KW|Wrath}}. This will give you the 3 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''' benefit from entering {{KW|Divinity}}, and counts as two {{KW|Stance}} switches.

* {{BD|Draw Card}} will activate after drawing cards regularly at the start of your turn, and after any possible {{BD|Rushdown}} draws cards as a result of having entered {{KW|Wrath}} through {{BD|Simmering Rage}}. This means that having excess {{BD|Draw Card}} will end up simply being wasted.

=== Synergies ===
* When entering {{KW|Wrath}} if you are not in {{KW|Wrath}} yet:
** If you have {{BD|Rushdown}} from {{C|Rushdown}}, you will draw that many cards.
** You will switch {{KW|Stance}}, which results in the following:
*** Any {{C|Flurry of Blows}} that was in your discard pile will be brought back to your hand, as long as there is space in hand.
*** {{C|Mental Fortress}} will give {{KW|Block}}.
*** If you were in the {{KW|Calm}} {{KW|Stance}} before, you will gain 2 {{Icon|PE}} '''Energy''', or 3 if you have {{R|Violet Lotus}}.

* Being in {{KW|Wrath}} changes the effects of some cards:
** {{C|Halt}} will give its additional {{KW|Block}}.
** {{C|Indignation}} will apply {{BD|Vulnerable}}.

=== Neutral ===
* While in {{KW|Wrath}}, all {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attack}} damage you deal is doubled, but you also take double damage from enemy attacks.{{KW|Wrath}} only doubles damage from {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Attack|Attacks}}, not from effects such as {{BD|Panache}} or {{BD|Thorns}}, or relics such as {{R|Mercury Hourglass}}.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* As {{KW|Wrath}} is worse than the {{KW|Divinity}} {{KW|Stance}} in every way except for the aformentioned ones, using {{C|Simmering Fury}} while in {{KW|Divinity}} is generally bad.

== Trivia ==
* In the game code, Simmering Fury is called Vengeance.

{{C|Static Discharge}} is a 1 {{Icon|BE}}-cost {{QueryLink|Cards|color:Blue|Defect}} {{QueryLink|Cards|rarity:Uncommon|Uncommon}} {{QueryLink|Cards|type:Power|Power}}. <!---Once played, it will {{KW|Channel}} 1 (2) {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} whenever you receive {{KW|Block|unblocked}} attack damage from an enemy.--->

== Interactions ==
=== Order ===
* Static Discharge will {{KW|Channel}} the Orb ''immediately'' upon receiving the damage, before the enemy turn can continue. This can {{KW|Evoke}} Orbs in the middle of an attack:
** If a {{KW|Lightning}} or {{KW|Dark}} Orb is Evoked, the damage can kill an enemy. If it is the enemy currently attacking, it will die immediately, ending the attack even if there were additional hits remaining. 
*** If an enemy dies this way while you have {{R|Gremlin Horn}} (and the combat does not end), you will receive {{Icon|BE}} and draw cards after the current attack has concluded. The cards will be kept until your next turn, while the {{Icon|BE}} will be lost unless you have {{R|Ice Cream}}.
** If a {{KW|Frost}} Orb is Evoked, the {{KW|Block}} will be applied immediately. This will reduce subsequent damage, even if those are further hits of the same attack. 
** If a {{KW|Plasma}} Orb is Evoked, the {{Icon|BE}} it generates will be lost, unless you have {{R|Ice Cream}}.

=== Synergies ===
* Static Discharge is particularly effective in fights with multi-hit attacks, especially including [[Hexaghost]], [[Byrd|Byrds]], [[Book of Stabbing]], and the [[Corrupt Heart]]
* {{R|Torii}} and {{R|Tungsten Rod}} can both decrease the amount of damage you receive while still allowing Static Discharge to trigger.

==== General Orb Synergies ====
* Other Orb sources, such as {{C|Darkness}} and {{C|Coolheaded}}, can be very helpful for {{KW|Evoke|Evoking}} {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} more frequently.
* {{C|Thunder Strike}} hits more times for each {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orb}} {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} this combat, and {{C|Electrodynamics}} makes {{KW|Lightning|Lightning Orbs}} hit all enemies.
* Sources of {{BD|Focus}} will improve the effects of Orbs: {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Consume}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{R|Data Disk}}
* Sources of additional Orb Slots allow for having more [[Orbs#Passive|Orb Passives]] in parallel: {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, {{P|Potion of Capacity}}
* {{C|Bullseye}} applies {{BD|Lock-On}}, which makes damaging Orbs deal 50% more damage to that enemy.
* {{C|Compile Driver}} draws a card for each unique type of Orb {{KW|Channel|Channeled}}.
* {{C|Barrage}} deals damage for each {{KW|Channel|Channeled}} Orb, while {{C|Fission}} draws a card and adds 1 {{Icon|BE}} for each Channeled Orb.
* {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}}, and {{C|Multi-Cast}} each can directly {{KW|Evoke}} your Orbs 1, 2, or X times respectively.

=== Neutral ===
* Static Discharge will only {{KW|Channel}} Orbs when taking attack damage. Other sources of enemy damage such as {{BD|Thorns}} and {{BD|Beat of Death}} will not trigger it.
* Static Discharge requires you to actually take damage to trigger: if an enemy is doing 0 damage (perhaps due to having negative {{BD|Strength}}), it will not trigger even if you have 0 {{KW|Block}}.
** Similarly, damage prevented with {{BD|Buffer}} will not trigger Static Discharge.
** However, as {{R|Tungsten Rod}} reduces ''HP Loss'', rather than damage, it is possible to lose no HP while triggering Static Discharge, if the attack would have done precisely 1 unblocked damage.

=== Anti-Synergies ===
* {{C|Reprogram}} and {{C|Hyperbeam}} give negative {{BD|Focus}}, making {{KW|Lightning}} Orbs less effective.

Static Discharge card now clarifies that it triggers when you receive unblocked attack damage.
